newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate issuance seen heavy this week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate issuance seen heavy this week.

text.p: A strong rally in the U.S. Treasury bond market last week has resulted in a large number of U.S. corporate borrowers looking to tap the market this week, taking advantage of yields not seen since the Federal Reserve raised interest rates in March, market sources said.
"It's hard to gauge right now what will happen today but there seems to be a very large calendar developing for the week," said one syndicate source at a U.S. investment bank.
Market sources said they expect approximately $2.5 billion of new corporate debt issuance to come to market this week.

"We had the rally last week and when the dust settled we were ahead of the game. Rates, although they are not ideal are getting a bit better and there is a very positive tone right now," said the syndicate source.
At 1045 EDT/1545 GMT, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was down 2/32 at 94.20 to yield 7.06 percent.
The biggest issues expected include Barrick Gold's $500 million 10-year issue via Goldman Sachs and Tenaga Nacionale's $500 million 10-year yankee bond via UBS Securities.
Market sources said unofficial price talk on Barrick Gold is 60 basis points over Treasuries.
Also expected this week is Credit Suisse First Boston's 500 million offering of step-up perpetual bonds.
Tenneco is expected to issue a 2-part $300 million issue consiting of 100 million of 10-year notes and $200 million 30-year bonds via Merrill Lynch.
G-Tech is expected to issue $300 million of debt consisting of $150 million seven-year notes and $150 million of 10-year notes via Credit Suisse First Boston.
The unofficial market talk on the 7-year tranche is for 80 basis points over and 90 basis points over on the 10-year.
Transocean Offshore is expected to issue $200 million of 30-year bonds and $100 million of 30-year bonds with a 10-year put option via Goldman Sachs.
Meanwhile, SK Telecom is expected to issue $230 million of 10-year yankee notes via Merrill Lynch.
A market source said unofficial price talk for SK Telecom is 90 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
Another issue expected to come to market but not until early May is Norfolk and Southern's $3.0 billion offering.
"Right now it looks as though Norfolk and Southern will be $3.0 billion but it might even be bigger," said one source.
In the high yield area, L-3 Communications is expected to issue $200 million of 144-A senior sunordinated noted due 2007 via Lehman Brothers.
Later this week, Neenah Corp is expected to issue $140 million 144-A senior subordinated notes due 2007 via Chase Securities.
Additionally, KSL Recreation Group Inc is expected to issue $125 million 144-A senior subordinated notes due 2007.
